name: Sjörå
body:
SJÖRÅ
CR 9

This pale beauty has sweeping green hair, deep reflective eyes, and an otherworldly stillness about her.

XP 6,400
N Medium fey (water)
Init +8; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +19
Aura fascinating beauty (30 ft., DC 21)

DEFENSE

AC 23, touch 20, flat-footed 18 (+5 deflection, +4 Dex, +1 dodge, +3 natural)
hp 114 (12d6+72); fast healing 5 (underwater only)
Fort +9, Ref +12, Will +12
DR 10/cold iron; Immune cold; SR 20

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., swim 40 ft. (swim 60 ft. in fish form)
Melee dazing touch +10
Special Attacks captivating allure, warden’s misfortune
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 9th; concentration +14)

Constant—speak with animals (aquatic creatures only)
At will—fog cloud, water breathing
3/day—aqueous orb (DC 18), control water, hydraulic push, rising water
1/day—control weather

STATISTICS

Str 12, Dex 19, Con 20, Int 14, Wis 19, Cha 21
Base Atk +6; CMB +7; CMD 33
Feats Combat Casting, Defensive Combat Training, Dodge, Improved Initiative, Toughness, Weapon Finesse
Skills Bluff +20, Diplomacy +20, Handle Animal +17, Knowledge (nature) +17, Perception +19, Sense Motive +19, Stealth +19, Swim +24
Languages Aquan, Common, Sylvan; speak with animals (aquatic creatures only)
SQ change shape (humanoid or Medium-sized fish; polymorph), warden’s fortune, water melding

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Captivating Allure (Su)

A sjörå can lure a creature toward her. As a standard action, the sjörå targets a creature within 60 feet. That creature must succeed on a DC 21 Will saving throw or become fascinated for up to 10 minutes. A creature that successfully saves is immune to that sjörå’s captivating allure for 24 hours. A captivated creature moves toward the sjörå using the most direct means available. If this path leads into a dangerous area, such as a non-water breathing creature moving below the water’s surface, the creature receives a second saving throw to end the effect before moving into peril but otherwise can take no actions other than to defend itself. A victim within 5 feet of the sjörå simply stands and takes no actions. This is a mind-affecting charm effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Dazing Touch (Su)

When a sjörå hits a living creature with a melee touch attack, the touched creature must succeed at a DC 21 Will save or be dazed for 1d4 rounds. This is a mind?affecting compulsion effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Fascinating Beauty (Su)

Any creature sexually attracted to women that comes within 30 feet of a sjörå must succeed on a DC 21 Will save or become fascinated. A sjörå can suppress this ability or resume it as a free action. This is a mind?affecting compulsion effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Warden’s Fortune (Su)

A sjörå can grant a non-fey creature a boon of luck. The creature gains a +5 luck bonus on Profession (fisherman) checks, Survival checks in aquatic terrain, Profession (sailor) checks and Swim checks. The creature also gains a +1 luck bonus on all saving throws. This effect lasts for 1 year or until the sjörå dismisses it.

Warden’s Misfortune (Su)

A sjörå can curse a creature within 120 feet. The creature must succeed at a DC 21 Will save or it automatically fails any checks made to catch fish. Signs of this misfortune include nets mysteriously tearing and fish abandoning the area. A creature that succeeds on its save is immune to this ability for 24 hours. The sjörå can dismiss this misfortune as a standard action. This is curse effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

Water Melding (Sp)

As a standard action a sjörå can merge her form with water, effectively rendering her invisible (as per the invisibility spell) but only while underwater.

ECOLOGY

Environment lakes and rivers
Organization solitary or kine (1 sjörå plus 2d6 trollgädda)
Treasure standard

The sjörå (also sjöfru) is a feminine water spirit, the “Mistress of the Lake”. She serves as warden and keeper of a lake or pool and some powerful sjörå rule over an entire lake system. She may reward those who treat her with deference and punishes those who take more than they need or are disrespectful to her domain.

Many tales tell of sightings of a sjörå sitting by the water’s edge, an ethereally beautiful woman combing her sweeping green hair while contemplating her reflection in the lake’s sparkling surface. The sjörå’s form often hints that she is more than she seems. Some accounts mention a line of fish scales running down her back or the faint hint of gills on her neck. Others speak of a faint luminescence around her, a subtle play of light on her shimmering hair that has the reflected glow of moonlight on still water.

Some lake folk take sightings of a sjörå’s activities as signs. Sjörå hanging her laundry means a coming storm, while combing her hair promises calm water, and a sjörå weeping foretells an approaching tragedy.

Fisherfolk who treat a sjörå’s lake with respect by leaving offerings, keeping the water clean, and fishing with care are rewarded with good fishing luck and safe passage.

Those who overfish, disturb the lake’s quiet, or foul the water suffer misfortune and lose their fishing luck entirely.

Those who show true disrespect to the sjörå herself suffer a darker fate. Sjörå can stir calm waters into a sudden tempest or lure the offender into the murky depths, never to surface again.

Sjörås often tend herds of large, pike?like fish called trollgäddor, treating them as favored pets. Sjörå hangs small bells around their necks, earning them the title skällgäddor (“bell pikes”). On rare occasions she places a crown on one of these great fish, and these krongäddor (“crown pikes”) are regarded as her most treasured possessions. Anyone who catches an abnormally large pike fish, especially one with a bell or crown, should return it to the water immediately lest they attract sjörå’s wrath.
